acceptance: A test terminates a preflight run (SIGTERM during the host-lock wait or before the pytest step) and asserts the receipt's status is not 'passed'.

A receipt whose recorded steps omit a step `verify_receipt` would require is written with a non-passed status, and a test pins this with the same required-step rule that `verify_receipt` uses (one shared function, not a copy).
`make pr-open` still refuses an incomplete receipt and accepts a complete one; existing preflight_receipt tests pass unchanged.
The item records the reproduced exit status for SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP before and after the fix.
context: Evidence from 2026-11-20: the receipt was for tree a15722be933a9cee3f2346c9156b4a28cea61a96 (branch chore/review-omp-pin-18.20.0, later #4411), cached under ~/.cache/benchbox/preflight/. It was moved aside and later lost with /tmp, so gate 1 must reproduce it. A preflight of the same tree, re-run after the lock was released, gave a complete receipt (1435 passed) and #4411 merged.
description:
Problem: scripts/preflight_receipt.py `finalize` sets `status` from `overall(steps)` whenever the recorded exit status is 0 (line ~315). `overall` passes if every *recorded* step is accepted, so it never checks that the steps the tree needed actually ran. On 2026-11-20 a `make pr-preflight` run was stopped by an outer job time limit while it waited for the host lock. It still wrote a receipt with `status: passed`, `exit_status: 0` and only changelog-check, docs-reference-inventory, project-references and theseus-prefetch steps: no `pytest` step, although the tree changed test files.

Current guard: `verify_receipt` (line ~406) adds `pytest` / `linux-pytest` to the required steps, so `make pr-open` refuses that receipt. The harm is a receipt file that claims a pass it never earned. Anything that reads `status` without calling `verify` (dashboards, a future consumer, a person) is misled. It is also unclear why the trap recorded exit 0 for a killed run.

Decision gates:
1. Before changing code, reproduce the termination: run pr-preflight on a tree with test changes, send SIGTERM (and separately SIGINT and SIGHUP) to the make process during the host-lock wait, and record which exit status the EXIT trap passes to `finalize`. If the recorded status is non-zero in every case, the remaining fix is only gate 2; say so on this item.
2. Choose where the completeness rule lives: `finalize` computes the same required-step set `verify_receipt` uses, or the receipt gets a separate 'complete' flag. Prefer one shared function so the two cannot drift.

Guardrails: do not weaken `verify_receipt`, which stays the gate pr-open trusts. Do not move, delete or recreate the host lock, and do not set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK or HEAVY_ADMIT=force in tests. Use a fake lock or a fixture. Keep existing receipt files readable: a receipt written before the fix must still verify or refuse exactly as today.
drop_reason: Duplicate of preflight-receipt-passes-when-killed-20261125; its root-cause analysis, decision gates and the SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP reproduction requirement are copied into that item's context and acceptance.
